_about: Sources named in editorial/items.json (disagreements and extra citations). Wiki references are numbered separately in sources/sam-wiki/extract.json. Every entry here was looked up on 2026-10-21; 'checked' says how.

nhlbi-guide.citation: National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute. Your Guide to Healthy Sleep. NIH Publication No. 11-5271 (2011).
nhlbi-guide.checked: Page numbers come from the health-glossary drafts (data/ai/sleep/nhlbi-*.json), which were hand-drafted from the PDF.

huberman-sleep-toolkit.license: Copyrighted; cited only, wording not reused
huberman-sleep-toolkit.checked: Claims flagged NOT VERIFIED in the glossary review notes were not checked here either.

hartstein-2024.citation: Hartstein LE, Mathew GM, Reichenberger DA, et al. The impact of screen use on sleep health across the lifespan: A National Sleep Foundation consensus statement. Sleep Health. 2024;10(4):373-384.
hartstein-2024.checked: Abstract read via PubMed. Panel reached consensus on 5 of 10 statements: screen use in general, and pre-bedtime content, impair sleep health in children and adolescents; behavioral strategies may reduce the effects. The abstract reports no consensus statement for adults or for pre-bedtime light.

bauducco-2024.citation: Bauducco S, Pillion M, Bartel K, Reynolds C, Kahn M, Gradisar M. A bidirectional model of sleep and technology use: A theoretical review of How much, for whom, and which mechanisms. Sleep Medicine Reviews. 2024;76:101933.
bauducco-2024.checked: Abstract read via PubMed. Theoretical review: the link runs both ways (sleep problems can lead to pre-sleep technology use, e.g. as a time filler or to regulate emotions); effects depend on how much, for whom, and which mechanism. Conflict of interest declared: Gradisar is CEO of WINK Sleep and employed by Sleep Cycle AB.

grandner-2025.citation: Grandner MA, Dzierzewski JM, Gozal D, Lopos JG, Miller AN, Redline S. Screen use and sleep health in children, adolescents, and adults: National Sleep Foundation consensus considerations and practical suggestions. Sleep Health. 2025;11(5):560-561.
grandner-2025.checked: Found via PubMed; no abstract. Not read. Listed because it is NSF's practical follow-up to the 2024 consensus.

do-one-thing.citation: Health Culture Foundation. Do One Thing: Choose your ONE THING (Habits by Category). SleepLiteracy.org, retrieved 2026-10-21.
do-one-thing.checked: Snapshot in sources/do-one-thing/habits.json. HCF's own campaign copy; its claims are not independently checked.
